newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks amble to firmer close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks amble to firmer close.

text.p: A mixed Australian share market ended in firmer territory on Tuesday but well off its early Dow-inspired highs as initial enthusiasm abated.
The All Ordinaries index added 6.4 points to 2,468.3 after touching an intraday high of 2,476.3.
Brokers said that while the market had made a strong start, there had been insufficient interest to maintain the momentum.
"It started off full of fight but it ran out of puff," said a senior dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.
"There is a bit of activity out there but it is all two-way business. There is not really much that is affecting prices," said Jamie Spiteri, dealer at Shaw Stockbroking.

News Corp's preferred ordinary shares topped turnover lists with nearly 43 million worth A$245 million (US$193.6 million) traded. The bulk of it was in six lines totalling 40 million specialled through First Pacific Stockbroking.
Market speculation centred on U.S. investor Ron Perelman lightening the swag of News preferred ordinary ADRs he received when News acquired New World Communications last year.
News ordinary shares received a fillip with the perceived overhang gone, jumping over two percent to A$6.84.
Building material stocks lost some recent gains as last week's highs proved too tempting for profit-takers.
Pioneer International ended six cents lower at A$4.14, CSR lost 13.9 cents to A$4.811 while Boral lost three to A$3.85.
Rises shaded falls just by a whisker, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
